interest: Shows 1949 debate on civilianizing SCAP and McDiarmid's critique of Dodge's counterpart-fund inflation analysis, tied to Cold War diplomacy.
overview: McDiarmid's June 1949 letter to Dodge discusses restructuring SCAP as a civilian authority like Germany's High Commission, critiques Dodge's counterpart-fund inflation memo, notes his CFM work on German currency and Austria, and encloses his Far Eastern Survey article on the yen exchange rate.

subfiles.about: Orville J. McDiarmid discusses Joseph M. Dodge's inflation memorandum, occupation administration streamlining, counterpart fund management, and international negotiations at the Council of Foreign Ministers.
subfiles.from: Orville J. McDiarmid, Associate Chief, Division of Financial Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: McDiarmid praises Dodge's inflation memo, discusses modeling SCAP on Germany's civilian High Commission, argues counterpart-fund investments don't necessarily expand money supply, reports on CFM work in Paris over German currency and Austria, and encloses his article on Japan's exchange rate.
